implementation_notes.patch_description: v10 stacks v6's cap=8 (which gave standalone Sharpe -0.36) with v9's Stage 3 strict (which gave -1.05). If the levers are independent and additive, expect mid-pack Sharpe; if super-additive (the gains compound), expect Sharpe better than either; if sub-additive (the levers fight each other), expect worse than either.

modified_s15_standalone.notes: v10 = SUB-ADDITIVE stack. Standalone Sharpe -1.59 is WORSE than either lever individually: v6 cap=8 alone gave -0.36, v9 Stage 3 strict alone gave -1.05. The combined effect is roughly v6+v9 (sub-additively) — the levers do NOT compound, they fight each other. Trade count 476 is between v6 (524) and v9 (576). Per-trade avg_pnl dropped to 0.0015 — the lowest of any version using cap≤8 — strong evidence that AND-logic Stage 3 + cap-based concentration are pruning DIFFERENT but OVERLAPPING populations: applying both simultaneously removes diversifying low-conviction trades that the cap alone would have kept (via ranking) and that Stage 3 strict alone would have kept (because more positions are allowed to clear the cap=20 cap). MaxDD held tight at 3.45% (~v9's 3.40%). Return collapsed to +0.69% (worst of the post-v3 stretch).

ablation_root_cause_analysis.v10_stack_effect: Stacking v6's cap=8 with v9's Stage 3 strict produced WORSE risk-adjusted return than either lever individually. The two filters are NOT independent — they prune overlapping populations of low-conviction trades. Applying both simultaneously over-prunes the diversifying tail and concentrates surviving trades into a narrower, more temporally-correlated set. This is the same loser-correlation failure mode that hurt v6 alone and v8 alone, amplified by the additional Stage 3 prune. Confirms: the productive lever is concentration via cap, NOT conviction-filter strictness, and the cap sweet-spot is cap=5 (v7) — NOT a cap that gets compounded with strictness.

standalone.v10_changes_vs_v6_and_v9: Stack of v6 cap=8 + v9 Stage 3 strictness. Result: SUB-ADDITIVE. Standalone Sharpe -1.59 is WORSE than v6 alone (-0.36) AND worse than v9 alone (-1.05). The levers fight each other: cap prunes by ranking, Stage 3 strict prunes by conviction; together they remove overlapping diversifying trades and over-concentrate the surviving population. avg_pnl per trade dropped to 0.0015 (lowest of any post-v3 version). The compound failure rules out 'combine multiple modest levers' as a productive direction. Final ranking on the standalone-Sharpe axis: v7 (+0.58) > v4 (+0.28) > v1 (+0.14) > v6 (-0.36) > v8 (-0.74) > v9 (-1.05) > v5 (-1.39) > v10 (-1.59) > v2 (-1.60) > v3 (-3.44).

computed_suggestion_rationale: Three of six gates pass (G2, G4, G6) and three fail (G1, G3, G5). v10 standalone Sharpe (-1.59) is the second-worst of 10 versions, beaten only by v3 (-3.44). The lever stack is sub-additive — combining v6's cap=8 with v9's AND-logic Stage 3 strictness produced WORSE risk-adjusted return than either lever alone. Combined Sharpe is also negative (-1.35). Confirms: the productive direction for this strategy is the concentration cap axis ALONE, with sweet spot at cap=5 (v7). No further lever combinations are likely to push past v7's standalone Sharpe of +0.58 within the 6-month window on the available data depth. KILL.
